Question: What is DRS
Answer: DRS stands for Drag Reduction System. It opens a flap in the rear wing to cut drag and give a following car extra speed for overtaking.

Question: What is DRS in F1

Question: What does DRS do
Answer: DRS opens a flap in the rear wing which reduces drag and increases top speed on straights to help a driver overtake.

Question: How does DRS work
Answer: A driver within one second of the car ahead can open the rear wing flap in designated DRS zones. This reduces drag and boosts top speed.

Question: When can DRS be used
Answer: DRS can only be used in designated zones once a driver is within one second of the car ahead and the race is under normal racing conditions.

Question: What is ERS in F1
Answer: ERS is the Energy Recovery System. It captures energy from braking and exhaust heat and redeploys it as extra electric power.

Question: What is KERS
Answer: KERS was the Kinetic Energy Recovery System that stored braking energy and gave a short power boost. It was replaced by the wider ERS.

Question: What is a power unit in F1
Answer: A power unit combines a combustion engine with electric energy recovery systems to drive the car.

Question: What is downforce
Answer: Downforce is the aerodynamic force that pushes the car onto the track so it can corner faster.

Question: What is slipstream
Answer: Slipstream is the pocket of reduced air resistance behind a car. A following driver gets pulled along and can close the gap.

Question: What is the halo in F1
Answer: The halo is a protective titanium structure above the cockpit that shields the driver's head from debris and impacts.

Question: What is a Grand Prix
Answer: A Grand Prix is a single race of the Formula 1 World Championship held at a circuit in a particular country or city.

Question: What is pole position
Answer: Pole position is the first place on the starting grid. It is awarded to the driver with the fastest lap in qualifying.

Question: What is qualifying in F1
Answer: Qualifying decides the starting grid. It has three knockout sessions called Q1 and Q2 and Q3 and the fastest driver in Q3 takes pole.

Question: What is a sprint race
Answer: A sprint is a shorter race of about 100 km held on some race weekends. It awards points to the top finishers and sets up a separate main race.

Question: How long is an F1 race
Answer: A Grand Prix is run over a distance of at least 305 km and has a maximum time limit of two hours. Monaco is shorter at about 260 km.

Question: What is a formation lap
Answer: The formation lap is the lap before the race start where drivers warm up their tyres and brakes and then line up on the grid.

Question: What is a pit stop
Answer: A pit stop is when a driver enters the pit lane to change tyres or repair the car and then rejoins the race.

Question: How long does a pit stop take
Answer: A typical pit stop takes about two to three seconds to change all four tyres.

Question: What is the pit lane speed limit
Answer: The pit lane speed limit is usually 80 km/h and is lower at some circuits such as Monaco.

Question: What is a DNF
Answer: DNF means Did Not Finish. It is recorded when a driver retires or fails to complete the race.

Question: What is a drive through penalty
Answer: A drive through penalty forces the driver to go through the pit lane at the speed limit without stopping which costs a lot of time.

Question: What penalties are there in F1
Answer: Penalties include time penalties of five or ten seconds and drive through penalties and grid drops and in serious cases disqualification.

Question: What is the virtual safety car
Answer: The virtual safety car makes all drivers slow to a set speed without bunching the field. It is used for incidents that do not need a full safety car.

Question: What is an undercut in F1
Answer: An undercut is when a driver pits earlier than a rival and uses fresh tyres to set faster laps so they come out ahead after the rival stops.

Question: What does a yellow flag mean
Answer: A yellow flag warns of danger on the track. Drivers must slow down and cannot overtake in that area.

Question: What does a red flag mean
Answer: A red flag means the session or race is stopped because of an accident or unsafe conditions.

Question: What does a blue flag mean
Answer: A blue flag tells a driver that a faster car is about to lap them and they must let it pass.

Question: What does the chequered flag mean
Answer: The chequered flag signals the end of the race or session.

Question: What does a black flag mean
Answer: A black flag disqualifies a driver who must return to the pits.

Question: What does a green flag mean
Answer: A green flag means the track is clear and racing can resume after a hazard.

Question: What are the F1 tyre compounds
Answer: Dry tyres come as soft and medium and hard compounds and are marked red and yellow and white. Intermediate tyres are green and full wet tyres are blue.

Question: What are intermediate tyres
Answer: Intermediate tyres are green marked tyres used on damp or lightly wet tracks. They have some grooves to clear water.

Question: What are the different tyre colours in F1
Answer: Red is soft and yellow is medium and white is hard. Green is intermediate and blue is full wet.

Question: What is the constructors championship
Answer: The constructors championship ranks teams by the total points scored by both of their drivers over the season.

Question: What is the drivers championship
Answer: The drivers championship is won by the driver with the most points at the end of the season and the winner becomes world champion.

Question: What is a team principal
Answer: The team principal is the person who runs an F1 team and is in charge of its strategy and management.

Question: What is the paddock
Answer: The paddock is the area at a circuit where teams and drivers and media and guests work behind the pit garages.

Question: What is the Monaco Grand Prix
Answer: The Monaco Grand Prix is held on tight streets in Monte Carlo. It is one of the most famous races and overtaking is very difficult there.

Question: What is Monza
Answer: Monza is Italy's historic circuit near Milan. It is known as the Temple of Speed because of its long straights and very high average speeds.

Question: What is Spa-Francorchamps
Answer: Spa-Francorchamps is the Belgian circuit in the Ardennes. It is the longest circuit on the calendar and is known for the Eau Rouge corner.

Question: What is Silverstone
Answer: Silverstone is the home of the British Grand Prix. It hosted the first ever Formula 1 world championship race in 1950.

Question: What is Formula 1
Answer: Formula 1 is the highest class of international single seater racing and its drivers and teams compete for world championships each season.

Question: Why is it called Formula 1
Answer: The word formula refers to the set of rules that all teams and cars must follow.
